title: The Best Marathons and Half Marathons in Thailand
seo_title: Best Marathons and Half Marathons in Thailand, From Results Data
meta_description: Thailand's marathons and half marathons compared from official results: field sizes, finish times and fees, with picks from Bangkok's ATMB to Khun Dan, Korat, Udon21 and Laguna Phuket.
dek: Official results from seven Thai races, about 74,000 finishers in all, show where Thailand's biggest and fastest fields are, what entry costs, and why most of the calendar falls between October and February.

sections.heading: What the Results Show
paragraphs: Run SEA holds official results for seven Thai races, about 74,000 finishers across editions from 2019 to 2026 [1]. The largest is the 2025 Amazing Thailand Marathon Bangkok (ATMB): 5,837 marathon finishers, 17,770 half-marathon finishers and 14,491 in the 10 km. That half-marathon field is the biggest of any race edition in our results for Southeast Asia, ahead of the 14,817 half-marathon finishers at the 2026 Singapore marathon weekend [1][2].

Thai marathon fields are quicker than the regional norm. Across 25 Southeast Asian marathons in our 2026 data, the median finish is 5:25 and 11% of finishers break four hours [2]. The 2025 ATMB median was 4:54, with 20% under four hours. Khun Dan's 2026 field matched it, at 4:54 and 19.5%, and Laguna Phuket's came in at 5:14 and 15% [1]. Only Vietnam's big-city marathons are faster in our data [2].

The half marathon is where Thailand stands out most. Six Thai half marathons from 2026, with 4,904 finishers between them, had a pooled median of 2:23, and 24.5% of finishers broke two hours. Across 74 half marathons region-wide the figures are 2:42 and 12% [1][2]. Women made up 28% of those Thai half-marathon finishers and 16% to 20% of Thai marathon finishers, close to the regional shares of 29% and 18% [1][2].

Entry is inexpensive. Of the 89 Thai race editions on our calendar, 59 list a fee range: the typical range runs from about THB 500 for the shortest distance to THB 1,200 for the longest, and for events with a marathon the top fee has a median of about THB 1,220 [3]. The ATMB sits at the top end, at THB 1,400 to 1,800 for the marathon depending on when you enter, plus a THB 50 booking fee [4].

sections.heading: When to Race: October to February
paragraphs: Of those 89 race editions, 72 (81%) fall between October and February. December is the busiest month, with 20 races, and the calendar has none in March, April or July [3]. That window is Thailand's cool season: the Thai Meteorological Department declares winter once minimum temperatures across upper Thailand stay below 23°C, which normally happens around mid-October, and the season generally lasts into mid-February [10].

Cool is relative, so start times stay early. The ATMB marathon starts at 2am and its half marathon at 4am [4], Korat's marathon at 3am [6] and Khun Dan's at 3.30am [7]. Outside the season the calendar thins to a handful of races in May and June, with Laguna Phuket the best known.
The upcoming Thai marathons and half marathons listed below this article update from the Run SEA calendar, so dates and fees there are current.

sections.heading: Bangkok: The ATMB and the Bangkok Marathon
paragraphs: For one big-city Thai marathon, the ATMB is the pick. It is co-organised by the Royal Thai Government, the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration, the Royal Thai Police and World Athletics, among others. The marathon, 10 km and 4.5 km start and finish at Sanam Luang, in front of the Supreme Court in the old city, and the half marathon runs the day before from MBK Center. The organiser's site lists the half marathon as a World Athletics Elite Label distance [4]. Demand is high: registrations for the 2025 edition passed 48,000 within a week [5]. Race details are at runsea.run/race/amazing-thailand-marathon-bangkok-atmb-2026/.

The results describe a broad field, not a slow one. The 2025 marathon median of 4:54 was about half an hour faster than the regional median, and women made up 30% of half-marathon finishers and 47% of 10 km finishers [1][2].

Bangkok's other marathon is the Bangkok Marathon, organised by the Jogging Association of Thailand. It starts on Sanam Chai Road beside the Grand Palace in January, and its 37th edition lists entries from THB 550 to 1,250 [3]. It is the cheaper, lower-key alternative in the same part of the city.

sections.heading: Beyond Bangkok: Khun Dan, Korat and Buriram
paragraphs: Khun Dan Marathon, run around the Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam in Nakhon Nayok, is the surprise in the data. The course is not flat: the registration page gives an elevation figure of about 400 for the marathon [7]. Even so, its 2026 field posted a 4:54 median, level with the 2025 ATMB and 19 minutes quicker than Laguna Phuket [1]. The race has shrunk and sharpened. In 2019 it had 470 marathon finishers, with a 5:16 median and 8.5% under four hours; in 2026 it had 256, with a 4:54 median and 19.5% under four [1]. Entry is THB 1,000 to 1,200 for the marathon [7].

The Korat Marathon in Nakhon Ratchasima starts at the Thao Suranari Monument and finishes at Bung Ta Lue Water Park. Its site says the race holds a World Athletics Road Race Label for 2026, and it reported 15,335 runners in 2025 [6]. Marathon entry is THB 1,200 to 1,600 [6]. Run SEA does not yet hold its results.

The Buriram Marathon is the novelty pick. It starts on the Chang International Circuit motor-racing track and finishes inside Chang Arena, the Buriram United football stadium. It has run as a night race, and The Nation put its 2024 field at more than 30,000 runners [9].

sections.heading: Half Marathons for a Fast Time
paragraphs: The quickest Thai half marathons in our data are smaller provincial races. Udon21 in Udon Thani, a half marathon with 10 km and 5 km races alongside, had a 2026 median of 2:10, and 37% of its 260 finishers broke two hours, the best figures of any Thai half we hold [1]. Its entries run from THB 600 to 950 [3]. Naew Ubon Run in Ubon Ratchathani (750 finishers, a 2:15 median and 32% under two hours) and Sponsor Run Bangkok at the Rama VIII Bridge (1,293 finishers, 2:18 and 28%) come next [1].
For a big crowd rather than a quick time, the ATMB's Saturday half marathon is the choice. Its 2025 median was 2:32, with 18% under two hours [1].

sections.heading: Laguna Phuket: The Off-Season Option
paragraphs: The Laguna Phuket Marathon is held in June from Laguna Grove on Phuket's west coast. It has the longest results record of any Thai race we track: its organiser links results back to 2015 [8], and our data covers 2019 onwards. Its marathon field fell from 2,231 finishers in 2019 to 1,049 in 2022 and 603 in 2026. Its half-marathon field fell from 3,689 to 1,737 over the same years [1].

As it shrank, the field got faster. The marathon median moved from 5:27 to 5:14, and the share under four hours doubled, from 7.6% to 15.1% [1]. Laguna also draws more women than most Thai races, at 36% of its 2026 half-marathon finishers [1]. June is outside the cool season, so treat it as a hot-weather race. The next edition is at runsea.run/race/laguna-phuket-marathon-2027/.

faqs.question: When is the best time to run a marathon in Thailand?
faqs.answer: Between October and February. Of the 89 Thai race editions on the Run SEA calendar, 72 fall in those five months, and December is the busiest. That is Thailand's cool season, which normally starts around mid-October and lasts into mid-February. Marathons still start between 2am and 4am to avoid the heat.

faqs.question: Which is the biggest marathon in Thailand?
faqs.answer: By finishers in Run SEA's results data, it is the Amazing Thailand Marathon Bangkok. Its 2025 edition had 5,837 marathon finishers and 17,770 half-marathon finishers, the largest half-marathon field in our data for Southeast Asia. The marathon starts at 2am at Sanam Luang, and the half marathon runs the day before.

faqs.question: Are Thai races fast compared with the rest of Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Yes, faster than most. Six Thai half marathons from 2026 had a pooled median of 2:23, with a quarter of finishers under two hours. The region-wide figures are 2:42 and 12%. Thai marathon medians ran from 4:54 to 5:14, against 5:25 across 25 Southeast Asian marathons. Only Vietnam's big marathons were quicker.

Finish-time figures: data/finish-times (2026 editions) and data/finish-times-history (ATMB 2025; Khun Dan 2019, 2024, 2025; Laguna Phuket 2019-2025); medians rounded to the minute, sub-4 and sub-2 shares are the percentage of finishers, female shares are among finishers with a recorded gender. Calendar counts and fee ranges: data/entities (country Thailand, 89 editions, which include some races' 2026 and 2027 editions; fees as listed, which vary by entry phase).
